body:
## Summary

On a production hive-mind host (hive-mind 2.33.11, start-command 0.35.1, 193 GiB disk, 121 GiB used), **18 stopped docker-isolation task containers hold 57 GB** (73% of all container space). `hive-cleanup` does not report this space, cannot reliably detect the containers, misses some of them entirely, and has no way to remove failed containers once they are old enough. Everything below is still present on `main`.

Required behaviour:

1. `hive-cleanup` must reliably **see** every stopped task container, including resume containers and their snapshot images, together with their sizes.
2. It must be able to **remove stopped containers** (for example, failed ones older than a TTL, or all stopped ones), and remove a successful container that was somehow left behind.
3. **Active containers must never be touched**, not even with `--force` and `--docker-isolation all`. Several tasks were executing on this host while this was tested.

## 1. Container detection is flaky: in 2 of 12 runs it silently reports "(none detected)"

```
$ for i in 1 2 3 4; do for m in "--docker-isolation all" "--docker-isolation=all" ""; do hive-cleanup --dry-run --verbose $m | grep Summary; done; done
run1 [--docker-isolation all] docker keep 0, docker remove 0      <- nothing detected
run1 [--docker-isolation=all] docker keep 4, docker remove 17
run1 []                       docker keep 21, docker remove 0
run2 ... run3 ...             (all detected)
run4 [--docker-isolation all] docker keep 4, docker remove 17
run4 [--docker-isolation=all] docker keep 4, docker remove 17
run4 []                       docker keep 0, docker remove 0      <- nothing detected
```

The output then reads `🐳 Docker isolation containers (all): (none detected)`, which is indistinguishable from a clean host.

Root cause, in `src/cleanup.os.lib.mjs`:

```js
export function listDockerIsolationContainers() {
  const out = tryExec('docker', ['ps', '-a', '--format', '{{json .}}']);
  return out ? parseDockerPsJsonLines(out) : [];
}
```

- `--format '{{json .}}'` includes `.Size`, so Docker computes the writable-layer size of **every** container. On this host that takes **11–17 s** per call, close to the **20 s** `tryExec` timeout.
- While containers are being created or removed, the size computation fails transiently:
  ```
  $ docker ps -a --format '{{json .}}'      # rc=1 after 4 s
  Error response from daemon: snapshotter.Usage failed for 8d26d994413c...: lstat /var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs/snapshots/67...: no such file or directory
  ```
  (and earlier: `failed to retrieve container list: rw layer snapshot not found for container 467d8f38061a...`)
- `tryExec` ignores stderr and turns any failure or timeout into `null`, so the result is `[]` and the error is invisible.

Suggested fix:
- List with an explicit, size-free format: `docker ps -a --no-trunc --format '{{.ID}}\t{{.Names}}\t{{.State}}\t{{.Status}}\t{{.Image}}\t{{.CreatedAt}}'`. That returns in milliseconds and does not touch the snapshotter.
- Retry once or twice on a non-zero exit.
- If listing still fails, print `⚠️ docker ps failed: <stderr>` and exit non-zero, never "(none detected)".
- Get sizes separately and best-effort, per container (`docker inspect --size` / `docker ps -a -s --filter id=...`), and never let them block detection.

## 2. Resume containers and their snapshot images are never seen

`DOCKER_ISOLATION_SESSION_NAME_RE` (`src/cleanup.lib.mjs`) accepts only a bare UUID:

```js
const DOCKER_ISOLATION_SESSION_NAME_RE = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-...-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i;
```

start-command's in-place resume (`$ --resume <id> -- <command>`, `execution-resume.js`) creates:
- a container named `<uuid>-resume-<attempt>` (here `e6c1dd3f-3acd-475d-8df4-f45b75879a8b-resume-1`, exited 127), and
- an image `start-command-resume/<uuid>:<attempt>` from `docker commit` of the stopped container (here **4.43 GB unique**).

Neither appears in any `hive-cleanup` output, so the 4.4 GB image can never be reclaimed through hive-mind. Suggested fix: accept `^<uuid>(-resume-\d+)?$`. When a resume container is removed, also remove its `start-command-resume/<uuid>:<n>` image if no other container uses it, and report that image's unique size.

## 3. No sizes, no age limit: 57 GB of failed containers is invisible and kept forever

The default mode `succeeded` keeps every failed container "for debugging" with no limit. The summary line says only `docker keep 21, docker remove 0`, without bytes. Current state:

| container | session | size | exited | reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50e97f5c9e99 | 48959e41 | 15.0 GB | Oct 4 19:45 | Claude OAuth expired, OOM flag |
| 70e758f039a6 | 6ae8b300 | 9.4 GB | Oct 6 21:03 | auto-restart limit, OOM flag |
| d5d1b1c3ee6a | e3dcfc75 | 5.3 GB | Oct 7 08:12 | auto-restart limit, OOM flag |
| 8604b82eef79 | 59a02269 | 5.0 GB | Oct 6 16:09 | auto-restart limit |
| 36b814464019 | c2780290 | 4.7 GB | Oct 5 22:37 | Codex cyber-risk refusal |
| 989e5e1179fe + image | e6c1dd3f-resume-1 | 4.4 GB | Oct 7 09:54 | broken resume (`/claude: not found`), see separate issue |
| a7207adf9cc4 | d332adec | 3.6 GB | Oct 4 19:42 | Claude OAuth expired, OOM flag |
| d9a38c244727 | e6c1dd3f | 3.2 GB | Oct 7 09:42 | claude exit 137 (OOM) |
| 2a7b211a1b53 | bebf2e57 | 3.2 GB | Oct 4 19:41 | Claude OAuth expired, OOM flag |
| f5d7742daa74 | d47d4467 | 2.1 GB | Oct 4 19:43 | Claude OAuth expired, OOM flag |
| 9 more | | 5.6 GB | Oct 4 – Oct 7 | Codex `none` effort, Codex 401, Claude OAuth |

Every one of these has already had its failure log uploaded to the PR or issue (`--attach-logs`), so the container is the only thing left holding the disk.

Suggestions:
- Show size per container and total kept or removable bytes in the summary (`docker keep 21 (57.0 GB)`).
- Add an age limit: `--docker-isolation failed-older-than=48h` (or `--keep-failed-for 48h`), plus an env var for the bot. Then a periodic `hive-cleanup --force` can reclaim space automatically without losing fresh failures.
- Optionally save `docker logs` and `docker inspect` to the start-command log dir before `docker rm`. Also check the git state of `/tmp/gh-issue-solver-*` inside the container, so unpushed work is never lost.

## 4. `--force` must never touch an active container: close the time-of-check race

`planDockerIsolationCleanup()` correctly keeps `running` containers in every mode. The removal itself, however, is:

```js
return tryExec('docker', ['rm', '-f', containerName], ...)   // src/cleanup.os.lib.mjs
```

The plan is computed from a `docker ps` snapshot taken 60–80 s earlier; a full `hive-cleanup` run took 53–84 s here. start-command's in-place resume (`DOCKER_START`) restarts **the same stopped container**. If a recovery resumes a container between plan and removal, `docker rm -f` kills a live task.

Suggested fix:
- Re-inspect immediately before removal: `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}} {{.State.Restarting}} {{.State.Pid}}'` must be `false false 0`.
- Use `docker rm` **without** `-f`, which Docker refuses for a running container.
- Also skip any container whose session is `executing` in `$ --status`, or whose name or UUID appears in an active start-command execution.

With `--force` this guarantees active containers survive.

## 5. Successful-but-not-removed containers must also be cleaned (and flagged as a bug)

On this host start-command did its job: all **111** successful sessions logged `Container removed: <uuid> (exit 0, ...)`, and no exit-0 task container is left. If one is ever left (for example, a `docker rm` failure during start-command's finalizer, or a session that exits 0 after the host restarted), `hive-cleanup` should:
- remove it in the default mode (it already would, *if* detection works; see item 1), and
- log it as `⚠️ successful container was not removed by start-command (bug)` so the leak is visible.

## 6. Other `hive-cleanup` findings from the same run

- `🏃 Active tasks detected: 1` while 3–4 docker-isolation tasks were executing. Containers `053a048d…` and `c5334d43…` were listed only as "running docker-isolation task", without session info.
- `/tmp/start-command` (1.2 GB, 157 logs, the largest 90 MB) is "protected path" and never rotated. Suggestion: compress or delete logs of sessions that ended more than N days ago and whose container no longer exists.
- `/tmp/log-tmp-hive-mind-log-upload-*-sanitized-*` and `/tmp/log-home-box-hive-telegram-bot-*` (≈330 MB) are hive-mind's own log-upload staging clones, yet are reported as "not a recognised hive-mind artifact" and kept.

## Environment

- hive-mind 2.33.11 (also checked against `main`: items 1, 2 and 4 are unchanged in `src/cleanup.os.lib.mjs` and `src/cleanup.lib.mjs`)
- start-command 0.35.1; Docker 29.6.1 (host) and 29.8.0 (DinD, `fuse-overlayfs`)
- Related: #2294 (reclaim disk space with disk-space-saviour), link-foundation/disk-space-saviour#14 (dss cannot clean inside these DinD containers)
title: hive-cleanup: flaky docker-isolation detection (silent '(none detected)'), misses resume containers/images, no sizes or TTL for 57 GB of failed containers, rm -f race with active tasks
